record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: For hyperlight axions with mass below the present Hubble scale, can one develop position-space cosmic-microwave-background polarization observables that detect the quantized jump in polarization across an axion string and quantitatively characterize the sensitivity of upcoming CMB experiments to that jump?

evidence.quote: In particular, jumps of polarization across an axion string, measured in position space as opposed to spherical harmonic power spectra, are exactly quantized, and give us direct information about A. Measuring A = 1/9, for instance, will tell us that the electron is not the fundamental unit of electromagnetic charge! It will be very interesting to develop these position space observables for upcoming CMB experiments and characterize their sensitivity to this quantized jump.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hyperlight axion field $a$ with mass $m_a$ much less than the present-day Hubble scale $H_0$, coupled to electromagnetism via a Chern–Simons term
$$\mathcal{L} \supset \frac{A}{4\pi}\, \frac{a}{f_a}\, F_{\mu\nu}\tilde{F}^{\mu\nu},$$
where $f_a$ is the axion decay constant and $A \in \mathbb{Q}$ is the (rational) electromagnetic anomaly coefficient. Assume that, at the time of CMB last scattering or thereafter, a network of cosmic axion strings is present, around each of which the axion field winds by $2\pi$. As a linearly polarized CMB photon propagates from last scattering to an observer, its polarization angle is rotated by an amount proportional to the change in $a/f_a$ along its trajectory; consequently, comparing two nearby lines of sight that pass on opposite sides of an axion string yields a discontinuous, topologically quantized jump in the polarization angle equal to $\pi A$ (modulo $2\pi$).

Problem. Construct position-space (i.e., real-space, as opposed to spherical-harmonic power-spectrum) statistical observables built from the Stokes parameters $Q(\hat n), U(\hat n)$ of the CMB polarization field that:

(a) are sensitive to, and able to detect, the quantized jump $\pi A$ in the linear polarization angle across a putative axion string;

(b) allow one to estimate $A$ from CMB polarization maps (for example, distinguishing $A = 1$ from $A = 1/9$);

(c) admit a quantitative forecast of their signal-to-noise ratio, given a model of the axion-string network and the instrumental noise and angular resolution of a specified CMB polarization experiment.

Provide such observables together with explicit formulas characterizing their sensitivity.
artifact.status_search_result: The general framework (quantized polarization rotation around axion strings and its appearance as a birefringence signal in CMB statistics) is established, and subsequent works have computed E/B power spectra and proposed reconstruction methods for polarization-rotation maps from axion-string networks. However, fully developed position-space estimators specifically designed to detect the discrete quantized jump $\pi A$ across individual strings, together with quantitative forecasts of their sensitivity for upcoming CMB experiments, do not appear to have been fully delivered; the problem appears at most partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: A CMB Millikan experiment with cosmic axiverse strings
status_evidence.snippet: Quantized polarization rotation around axion strings; effect is topological, depends only on anomaly coefficient.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the quantized jump phenomenon and motivates CMB observables, but uses harmonic-space power-spectrum forecasts.

status_evidence.title: CMB birefringence from ultra-light axion string networks
status_evidence.snippet: Computes birefringence signal from ultra-light axion string networks in the CMB.
status_evidence.claim: Develops harmonic-space predictions; position-space jump estimators not fully constructed.

status_evidence.title: Probing cosmic strings by reconstructing polarization rotation of the cosmic microwave background
status_evidence.snippet: Reconstruction of polarization-rotation field from CMB to probe cosmic strings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward map-level/position-space detection of string-induced polarization rotation.
